learn.hook: Utsav time! Rangoli, flags and bead garlands all have patterns.
points: A pattern repeats again and again.
The part that repeats is the 'core'.
🔴🔵🔴🔵 repeats red, blue.
Patterns can use colours, shapes, sizes or sounds.
learn.reallife: Toran on doors, rangoli at Diwali and stripes on a kurta show patterns.

games.title: True or false?
items: Red, green repeats again and again.
A pattern must use only colours.
Shapes, sizes and sounds can make patterns too.
Clap, stamp, clap, stamp is a pattern.
No part repeats in the same order.

quiz.q: Which is a pattern?
quiz.explain: Red, blue repeats again and again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any mix of colours is a pattern

quiz.q: What repeats in 🔺⬛🔺⬛🔺⬛?
quiz.explain: A triangle then a square, again and again.

quiz.q: Riya makes a garland: 🌼🌼🌸🌼🌼🌸. What is the core?
quiz.explain: Two yellow flowers then one pink flower repeat.
quiz.mistake: Takes only part of the core

quiz.q: Arjun claps, stamps, claps, stamps. What is this?
quiz.explain: Clap, stamp repeats. That is a pattern.

quiz.q: How many shapes are in the core of ⭐🌙☀️⭐🌙☀️?
quiz.explain: ⭐🌙☀️ repeats. That is 3 shapes.
quiz.mistake: Counts all shapes instead of the core

quiz.q: Which rangoli row is NOT a pattern?
quiz.explain: 🟠🟡🟠🟠🟡🟡 does not repeat the same part again and again.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any colourful row is a pattern

teach.ask: Gappu: What makes a row of beads a pattern?
teach.praise: Yes! The same part repeats again and again!
teach.nudge: Does something happen again and again? What repeats?

learn.hook: Toran, flags and lights! Festivals are full of patterns.
points: At festivals we see patterns in flags, torans, garlands and lights.
A string of lights may go red, green, red, green.
To extend a pattern by colouring, find the core and colour it again and again.
A pattern keeps the same order every time.

example.q: A toran has 🥭🌼🥭🌼 ___ ___. Colour the next two.

learn.reallife: During Diwali, Pongal or Eid, look at the lights and paper flags. Can you spot the core?

games.title: True or false?
items: Lights going red, green, red, green make a pattern.
A pattern changes its order every time.
It repeats in the same order.
No part repeats in the same order.

quiz.q: Which toran is a pattern?
quiz.explain: 🥭🌼 repeats again and again.
quiz.mistake: Picks a row that has the same things but no fixed order

quiz.q: The lights go 🟡🔴🟡🔴🟡. What colour comes next?
quiz.explain: The core is 🟡🔴. After 🟡 comes 🔴.

quiz.q: Kites on a string: 🟥🟦🟦🟥🟦🟦🟥 ___ ___. Colour the next two.
quiz.explain: The core is 🟥🟦🟦. After 🟥 come two 🟦.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the core is just two colours

quiz.q: Paper flags go 🟩🟨🟩🟨. How many colours are in the core?
quiz.explain: The core is 🟩🟨: 2 colours.

quiz.q: Riya colours a garland: 🌸🌼🌼🌸🌼🌼. What is the repeating part?
quiz.explain: 🌸🌼🌼 comes again and again.

quiz.q: Where do we see patterns at Diwali?
options: In rows of diyas and strings of lights
quiz.explain: Diyas and lights are often in repeating rows.
quiz.mistake: Does not see patterns in everyday life

teach.ask: Gappu: My festival lights go 🔴🟡🟢🔴🟡. What colour do I put next?
teach.praise: 🟢 next! The core 🔴🟡🟢 repeats. So bright!
teach.nudge: Which part repeats? What came after 🟡 last time?

learn.hook: Patterns help us guess what comes next!
points: Find the part that repeats.
Say the pattern aloud.
Keep going in the same order.
Check by saying it again from the start.
learn.reallife: Lights on a Diwali string blink in patterns. We can guess the next colour!

quiz.q: Look at the beads. What comes next? 🔵🟡🔵🟡🔵 ___
quiz.explain: Blue, yellow repeats. After blue comes yellow.

quiz.q: Look at the sweets. What comes next? 🍬🍬🍫🍬🍬🍫🍬 ___
quiz.explain: Core is 🍬🍬🍫. After one 🍬 comes another 🍬.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the core is only two items

quiz.q: What comes next? clap, clap, jump, clap, clap ___
quiz.explain: Clap, clap, jump repeats. After two claps comes jump.

quiz.q: Meena strings beads: 🔴🟢🔵🔴🟢 ___. What is next?
quiz.explain: Red, green, blue repeats. After green comes blue.
quiz.mistake: Starts the core again too soon

quiz.q: What is missing? 🌸🍃🌸 ___ 🌸🍃
quiz.explain: Flower, leaf repeats. After 🌸 comes 🍃.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the item before the gap

quiz.q: Kabir's flag pattern is 🟧⬜🟩🟧⬜🟩. What are the next two?
quiz.explain: After 🟩 the pattern starts again: 🟧 then ⬜.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know what comes next in a pattern?
teach.praise: Find what repeats, then keep going. You did it!
teach.nudge: What part repeats? What comes after the last one?

learn.hook: Dip your thumb in paint and press! Let us print a pattern.
points: Dip your thumb in colour and press it on paper. That is a thumb print.
A finger print is smaller than a thumb print.
Make a pattern: thumb, finger, thumb, finger.
Fill your space with your own print pattern. Keep the same order.

example.q: Aisha prints thumb, finger, thumb, finger. What comes next?

learn.reallife: Thumb prints can make caterpillars, flowers and borders on greeting cards.

items.text: Red thumb, blue thumb, red thumb, ___

games.title: Pattern or not?
items: big, big, small, big, big, small
thumb, thumb, finger, finger, thumb, finger
red, red, blue, red, blue, blue
big, small, small, big, big, small

quiz.q: Riya prints thumb, finger, thumb, finger. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The core thumb, finger starts again.

quiz.q: Which print is bigger?
quiz.explain: The thumb is wider than the little finger.

quiz.q: Kabir prints 🟢🟢🟡🟢🟢🟡. What is the core?
quiz.explain: 🟢🟢🟡 repeats.

quiz.q: Meena prints 2 thumbs, then 1 finger, again and again. How many prints are in her core?
quiz.explain: 2 thumbs and 1 finger make 3.

quiz.q: Joseph prints his core 3 times: 👍☝️ 👍☝️ 👍☝️. How many prints in all?
quiz.explain: 2 prints, 3 times: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts the cores, not the prints

quiz.q: Which is a print pattern?
options: red, red, yellow, red, yellow, yellow
red thumb, yellow finger, red thumb, yellow finger
quiz.explain: Red thumb, yellow finger repeats.
quiz.mistake: Picks a row with no fixed order

teach.ask: Gappu: I printed big, small, big, small. What should I print next?
teach.praise: Big comes next! Big, small repeats. Pretty prints!
teach.nudge: What came after small last time?

points: 2, 4, 6, 8 goes up by 2 each time.
5, 10, 15, 20 goes up by 5 each time.
10, 9, 8, 7 goes down by 1 each time.
Find the jump, then keep going.
learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a road often go 2, 4, 6, 8.

quiz.q: What comes next? 2, 4, 6, 8, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 2. 8 + 2 = 10.

quiz.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 5. 15 + 5 = 20.

quiz.q: What comes next? 10, 9, 8, ___
quiz.explain: It goes down by 1. 8 - 1 = 7.

quiz.q: What is missing? 1, 3, ___, 7, 9
quiz.explain: It goes up by 2. 3 + 2 = 5.

quiz.q: Riya places diyas: 2, 4, 6, 8. How much does each step jump?
quiz.explain: 4 - 2 = 2. Each jump is 2.
quiz.mistake: Counts the steps instead of the jump

quiz.q: What comes next? 20, 30, 40, ___
quiz.explain: The jump is 10. 40 + 10 = 50.

teach.ask: Gappu: Someone said 2, 4, 6, 8. What comes next and why?
teach.praise: Jump by 2 each time. So 10 comes next!
teach.nudge: How much does each number jump? What do I add?

learn.hook: Doorsteps bloom with dots and lines! Let us make a kolam.
points: Kolam and rangoli are floor designs made at doorsteps.
A kolam is drawn with rice flour around a grid of dots.
Many kolams look the same on both sides, like butterfly wings.
To complete one, copy one side onto the other side.
Rangoli colours and shapes often repeat around the centre.

example.q: A kolam has a grid of 3 rows of 3 dots. How many dots?

learn.reallife: In many Indian homes, a kolam or rangoli is drawn at the door every morning or at festivals.

games.title: True or false?
items: Kolam is often drawn with rice flour.
A kolam is drawn around a grid of dots.
If a rangoli matches like a mirror, its two halves look different.
Rangoli colours often repeat around the centre.
A kolam grid of 2 rows of 4 dots has 6 dots.

quiz.q: A kolam has 3 rows of 3 dots. How many dots?
A rangoli is the same on both sides. The left side has a 🌸 at the top. What should the right side have at the top?
quiz.explain: Both sides match, so the right side also gets 🌸.
quiz.mistake: Does not copy the matching side

quiz.q: A kolam is usually drawn with ___.
quiz.explain: Kolam is drawn on the floor with rice flour.
quiz.mistake: Does not know how kolam is made

quiz.q: Around the centre, a rangoli goes 🔴🟡🔴🟡🔴 ___. What colour is next?
quiz.explain: The core is 🔴🟡. After 🔴 comes 🟡.

quiz.q: A kolam grid has 2 rows of 4 dots. How many dots?
Why do people draw kolam and rangoli?
quiz.explain: They are beautiful floor decorations.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what kolam is for

teach.ask: Gappu: I drew half a rangoli. How do I finish the other half?
teach.praise: Copy it like a mirror! Both halves match. Beautiful!
teach.nudge: What should the other side look like?

learn.hook: Look around! Patterns hide on leaves, tiles, sarees and zebras.
points: Arrange pebbles, flowers, leaves, bangles, coins or caps in a pattern.
Nature has patterns: a beehive, butterfly wings, zebra stripes.
Sarees, curtains and floor tiles have repeating designs too.
Look for the part that repeats.

example.q: Make a pattern with 2 caps and 1 coin. Show two cores.
steps: The core is cap, cap, coin.
example.answer: cap, cap, coin, cap, cap, coin

learn.reallife: Look at your school floor, your mother's saree border or a pineapple. Find the repeat!

quiz.q: Which one has a pattern in nature?
quiz.explain: Black and white stripes repeat on a zebra.

quiz.q: A beehive is made of many cells of the same shape. What shape are they?
quiz.explain: Honeycomb cells have 6 sides. That is a hexagon.

quiz.q: Riya arranges bangles: 🔴🔴🟢🔴🔴🟢. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The core 🔴🔴🟢 starts again with 🔴.

quiz.q: Where at home can you find a repeating pattern?
quiz.explain: Tiles repeat the same shape again and again.
quiz.mistake: Does not see patterns at home

quiz.q: A saree border goes 🔺🔻🔺🔻. How many shapes are in the core?
quiz.explain: The core is 🔺🔻: 2 shapes.

quiz.q: Kabir lines up 🪨🍃🪨🍃🪨🍃. How many pebbles?
quiz.explain: Each core has 1 pebble. 3 cores, so 3 pebbles.

teach.ask: Gappu: Where can I find patterns around me?
teach.praise: Tiles, sarees, beehives, zebras! Patterns are everywhere!
teach.nudge: Can you name one place where something repeats?

learn.hook: Clap, snap, stamp! Your body can make patterns too.
points: Cut out pictures of things with patterns, like tiles, cloth and leaves. Paste them on a sheet. That is a collage.
Patterns can be made with actions: clap, snap, stamp.
Clap, clap, stamp, clap, clap, stamp. The core is clap, clap, stamp.
Do the core again and again in the same order.

example.q: Clap, snap, stamp, clap, snap, stamp. What comes next?
steps: The core is clap, snap, stamp.

learn.reallife: Garba and dandiya dancers repeat steps in a pattern. Music has beats that repeat too.

games.title: Make a collage
items: Show your collage to the class

quiz.q: Clap, stamp, clap, stamp, clap. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The core is clap, stamp. After clap comes stamp.

quiz.q: Snap, snap, clap, snap, snap, clap. What is the core?
quiz.explain: snap, snap, clap repeats.

quiz.q: How many actions are in the core of clap, snap, stamp, clap, snap, stamp?
quiz.explain: The core is clap, snap, stamp: 3 actions.

quiz.q: Which is an action pattern?
options: jump, clap, clap, jump, jump, clap
quiz.explain: jump, clap repeats in the same order.
quiz.mistake: Picks a row with no fixed order

quiz.q: Meena pastes a tile picture and a saree picture on her sheet. What is she making?
quiz.explain: Pasting pattern pictures together makes a collage.
quiz.mistake: Does not know what a collage is

quiz.q: Arjun does clap, clap, stamp 3 times. How many claps in all?
quiz.explain: 2 claps each time: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

teach.ask: Gappu: Can I make a pattern without crayons, only with my wings and feet?
teach.praise: Flap, flap, stamp, again and again! An action pattern!
teach.nudge: Which actions will I repeat? In what order?
